---
title: "Derivation of the Exponential TDM Survival Formula"
format: html
---

We wish to derive the formula

$$
S \;=\;\exp\!\Bigl(-\sum_{i=1}^{n}\alpha\,e^{\beta\,T_i}\Bigr)
$$

which gives the cumulative egg-to-fry survival (S) over (n) days, each at temperature (T_i).

## 1. Instantaneous Mortality (Hazard) Rate

Assume that at water temperature (T) (in °C), the instantaneous daily mortality rate (hazard) is

$$
h(T) \;=\; \alpha \, e^{\beta\,T},
$$

where - (\alpha \> 0) is a baseline mortality coefficient,\
- (\beta) controls how sharply mortality increases with temperature.

## 2. Survival over a Small Interval

In continuous‐time hazard theory, the probability of surviving a small time interval (\Delta t) when the hazard is (h) is

$$
\exp\!\bigl(-\,h\,\Delta t\bigr).
$$

Taking (\Delta t = 1) day, daily survival at temperature (T) becomes

$$
\exp\!\bigl(-\,h(T)\times1\bigr)
\;=\;
\exp\!\bigl(-\,\alpha\,e^{\beta\,T}\bigr).
$$

## 3. Discrete Day-by-Day Survival

If each day (i=1,\dots,n) has temperature (T_i), and survival across days multiplies, then

$$
S
\;=\;
\prod_{i=1}^{n}
  \exp\!\bigl(-\,\alpha\,e^{\beta\,T_i}\bigr).
$$

## 4. Collapse the Product into a Single Exponential

Use the identity

$$
\prod_{i=1}^n e^{x_i}
\;=\;
e^{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}.
$$

Here (x_i = -\alpha,e\^{\beta T_i}), so

$$
\prod_{i=1}^n
  \exp\!\bigl(-\,\alpha\,e^{\beta\,T_i}\bigr)
=
\exp\!\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n -\,\alpha\,e^{\beta\,T_i}\Bigr)
=
\exp\!\Bigl(-\sum_{i=1}^n \alpha\,e^{\beta\,T_i}\Bigr).
$$

Hence the final result:

$$
\boxed{
S \;=\;\exp\!\Bigl(-\sum_{i=1}^{n}\alpha\,e^{\beta\,T_i}\Bigr)
}.
$$

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Intuitive Summary

-   **Hazard** (h(T)=\alpha e\^{\beta T}) means hotter days (larger (T)) exponentially increase daily mortality.\
-   **Daily survival** is (\exp(-h)).\
-   **Cumulative survival** is the product of daily survivals, which algebraically collapses to one exponential of the summed hazards.

## Derivation of the Linear Threshold TDM Survival Formula

We wish to derive the formula

$$
S \;=\;\exp\!\Bigl(-\alpha \sum_{i=1}^{n} \max(T_i - \beta,\,0)\Bigr)
$$

which gives cumulative egg-to-fry survival (S) over (n) days with daily temperatures (T_i), using a linear threshold mortality model with parameters (\alpha) and (\beta).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 1. Define the daily hazard (mortality) rate

Under the linear threshold model, on day (i) with temperature (T_i):

1.  Compute the daily "excess" above threshold (\beta): $$
    E_i \;=\;\max\bigl(T_i - \beta,\,0\bigr)\,.
    $$
2.  Assume hazard (mortality rate) on day (i) is proportional to this excess: $$
    h_i = \alpha \,E_i
         = \alpha \,\max(T_i - \beta,\,0),
    $$ where (\alpha) (units: day(^{-1})·°C(^{-1})) scales how strongly excess temperature drives mortality.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 2. Survival over one day

When the daily hazard is (h_i), the probability of surviving that day is

$$
\exp(-h_i\times1)
\;=\;
\exp\!\bigl(-\alpha\,E_i\bigr)
\;=\;
\exp\!\bigl(-\alpha\;\max(T_i - \beta,0)\bigr).
$$

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 3. Multiplying over all days

Assuming independence, survival over (n) days is the product of daily survivals:

$$
S
\;=\;
\prod_{i=1}^n
  \exp\!\bigl(-\alpha\,\max(T_i - \beta,0)\bigr)
\;=\;
\exp\!\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n -\,\alpha\,\max(T_i - \beta,0)\Bigr).
$$

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 4. Final closed‐form

Pulling the minus sign outside,

$$
\boxed{
S \;=\;\exp\!\Bigl(-\alpha \sum_{i=1}^{n}\max(T_i - \beta,\,0)\Bigr)
}.
$$

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Intuition

-   **Threshold** (\beta) means no mortality when (T_i \le \beta).\
-   **Excess** (E_i = \max(T_i-\beta,0)) drives hazard linearly.\
-   **Survival** is the exponential of minus the cumulative hazard (\sum\_i \alpha E_i).
